editorial_intent: Soluble Dll4 protein shed from endothelial lining binds to collagen I matrix, hyperactivating Notch2 receptors to strip capillary density and trigger sarcopenia.
subject: An isometric slice of aging skeletal muscle matrix showing an endothelial vessel wall shedding geometric Dll4 ligands that dock into striated collagen type I fibers and over-engage Notch2 receptor complexes, leading to capillary network pruning and myofibril fragmentation
setting: Constructivist frame incorporating a subtle 20% background motif of a hexagonal fourth-phase water crystal lattice with concentric hydration shells and four laminar drainage sluice vectors
composition: Asymmetric split-panel lithograph layout with a left-to-right causal sequence: intact vascularized muscle on the left transitioning across a diagonal terracotta barrier vector into a degraded, matrix-clogged microvascular landscape on the right
